question.text: In retirement income planning, the sequence of returns risk refers to:

answer.text: The order in which different investments mature
The risk that poor investment returns in the early years of retirement disproportionately deplete the corpus
The sequence in which the subscriber selects pension funds
The order of priority for paying expenses

explanation.text: The Logic: Sequence of returns risk is the risk that poor investment returns occurring early in the retirement-drawdown phase — when systematic withdrawals are already being made — disproportionately deplete the retirement corpus, even when the long-run average return over the full retirement horizon is otherwise adequate. The same average return can produce very different outcomes depending on when the bad years occur. The Trap: The risk is not about maturity ordering of investments, not about how a subscriber picks pension funds, and not about the order of paying expenses; those describe operational or planning matters, not the corpus-depletion risk created by early negative returns combined with withdrawals. Note: The exact named concept "sequence of returns risk" is not stated verbatim in the cited NISM Series XVII workbook pages, which discuss the bucket strategy, market recovery time, and early-withdrawal risk. The framing above reflects general retirement-income-planning theory rather than a direct workbook citation.
